PRE-SCAN AHEAD OF CLAIMING — which of this ticket's four earlier research findings still hold, checked against source at HEAD 44d9250ea. Recorded now because 0d76 is still blocked by 3768 and the point of this note is that PART OF THE EARLIER RESEARCH IS NOW STALE; acting on it would waste a very expensive run.

**FINDING 1 — STILL TRUE (verified).** "No new gate logic; wiring only" remains FALSE. `parity_report` has no caller outside `parity.py` itself: the only references under `src/` are its own definition, two internal reuses by `container_fidelity_report` (:213) and `prerequisite_fidelity_report` (:236), and a docstring mention in `parallel_run_and_diff` (:287). It is NOT exported from `rebar.llm` (empty grep of `llm/__init__.py`). So there is still no CLI path, no serializer, and no ItemRecord adapter — building the run_eval -> ItemRecord mapping is net-new, load-bearing work, because criterion (b) is scored on it.

**FINDING 2 — STILL TRUE (verified).** `parity.py:88` still sets `MIN_GOLD_ITEMS = 20` and it is the default of `parity_report(min_gold=...)`, so the gold-coverage floor still forces pooling across specs or an explicit, justified lower bound.

**FINDING 3 — not re-verified.** The claim that the corpus barely produces blocking verdicts is left standing; I did not re-measure it.

**FINDING 4 — NOW LARGELY STALE, and this is the substantive update.** It said the two arms would differ in TWO variables rather than one, for two reasons, and BOTH have since been closed by landed work:
* It cited `review_kernel/verify.py:269`'s equality rule (`verifier_default if model == default_model`) as meaning the Pass-2/Pass-4 downgrade would STOP APPLYING on the Bedrock arm. That mechanism is UNREACHABLE: `resolve_verifier_model` has ZERO callers under `src/rebar`, pinned by `tests/unit/test_code_review_verifier_class.py::test_the_superseded_equality_rule_has_no_production_consumers` (172e). The verifier paths resolve the `standard` CLASS instead. NOTE: I myself asserted the opposite earlier in this session and had to retract it — I had confirmed the function BODY still contains the expression and wrongly inferred the rule was live. Existence is not reachability.
* It cited `plan-review.yaml`'s ladder as BARE `claude-*` names, so a "Bedrock" run would still send Pass-1 to DIRECT ANTHROPIC. Also fixed: `:62-65` now reads `[trivial, standard, frontier]` (7761), and 3768 has just declared a class on every code-review LLM step (`base`/`round_a`/`round_b` -> frontier, `verify`/`coach` -> standard), so no pass inherits a single scalar any more.
Its REMEDY, however, still stands and is now ACHIEVABLE rather than aspirational: "the driver must pin per-pass models on BOTH arms explicitly". That is exactly what the class config now expresses.

**WORKING TWO-PROVIDER RECIPE, already exercised end-to-end on eb58 — reuse it rather than reinventing:** point `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` at a TOML carrying `[llm.model_classes]` with frontier on one provider and standard/trivial on the other (cb6f's pointer, so the checkout is never edited). A real `rebar review-plan` under that config produced **41 calls on `anthropic:claude-opus-4-8` + 1 call on `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`** — the same 41/1 per-pass split as the Anthropic-only baseline, with Pass-1 on one provider and the verifier on the other. Extract per-call counts ONLY from log lines carrying BOTH `model=` and `input_tokens=`; a whole-log grep for `bedrock:<model>` over-counts because verdict-JSON fields match too (it told me 4 when the truth was 1).

**TWO BEDROCK FACTS THIS RUN ESTABLISHED, both relevant to the parity protocol:**
1. **Bedrock REFUSES the plain model id on-demand.** `anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` fails with ValidationException: "Invocation of model ID ... with on-demand throughput isn't supported. Retry your request with the ID or ARN of an inference profile." The `us.`-prefixed INFERENCE PROFILE id works. Probe with an 8-token `aws bedrock-runtime converse` BEFORE funding a corpus run — the same mistake at N>=3 scale would burn the budget on ValidationExceptions.
2. **Prompt caching had NO effect on the Bedrock call** (`cache_read=0, cache_write=0` at 2857 input tokens) and rebar logged a warning saying so. Do not read that as a Bedrock caching regression without first accounting for bug 7a79 — the sub-4096-token cache warning is MISCALIBRATED and fires spuriously on BOTH providers.

COST SHAPE unchanged and still the main risk: ~3,200 model calls at N=3 across both arms, ~9h sequential, which exceeds the 6h GitHub-hosted job limit — shard per spec or split the job.
